Latin word

frūgī

frūgī (indecl.)

indeclinable adjective (an old dative of frūx); comparative frūgālior, superlative frūgālissimus

thrifty, frugal; honest, useful (of a person); plain, frugal; of a person, thrifty and sensible; good, well-behaved

In this lexicon

  • economy

    also used · classical · Cic. Deiot. 26: frūgī hominem dīcī nōn multum habet laudis in rēge (Lewis & Short s.v. frūx); Traupman 393

  • simple

    also used · classical · Mart. 13.31.1: jentācula … frūgī; Ter. Ad. 959: Frūgī homō es

  • well-behaved

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 99: frūgī es; Hor. Ep. 1.16.49: sum bonus et frūgī; Traupman 99; Traupman 322

  • frūgī bonae: well-behaved

    classical
